messages:
Ishaan: Heads-up — after the calibration sweep rolled out to mix-precision kernels (auto-steer enabled) we're seeing an eval delta on the structured-output eval set. High-level: token-level quality drop + intermittent hallucinations in JSON outputs.
Grace: Ugh. Which rollout? PR/flag?
Ishaan: Rollout is the new mixprecision_autosteer heuristic from #4567, enabled for prod-serving group B at 2023-11-02 04:12 UTC. Calibration profiles updated too (clip=0.995 -> 0.99).
Priya: Any perf regressions or just quality? Logs from the profiler would help.
Ishaan: Perf is weird — tail latency jumped ~8% on the canary, but majority of requests unaffected. Repro locally on latest runtime image when I force the same calib table.
Ryan: KV-cache telemetry shows increased cache churn for long-prefix inference. Eviction rate +15% on the canary nodes.
Marta: Could cache churn change numeric stability for quantized kernels? If KV cache alignment shifts, prefix scales might differ.
Priya: Possible. Also saw kernel switch counts spike: the steering code is preferring fp8 kernels for some layers, int4 for others, causing mixed-path rounding differences. Sharing quick profiler excerpt:
```
kernel_choice_counts: { fp8: 312k, int4: 205k, int8: 22k }
avg_latency_ms: { fp8: 7.1, int4: 5.8 }
batching_window_ms: 8 -> 12 (canary)
kv_hit_rate: 0.88 -> 0.75 (canary)
```
Grace: batching_window increased? That can mix sequence lengths and cause different kv cache placements.
Ishaan: Exactly. The autosteer logic added a small batching delay to favor fp8 packing; that increased cross-request mixing.
Ryan: When we mix fp8 and int4 in the same micro-batch, does the runtime mutate shared buffers differently? We saw a dtype-flip issue before.
Priya: Runtime uses separate code paths but shares the kv index allocator; there might be an ordering non-determinism leading to small quantization noise that cascades on structured-output decoders.
Marta: The hallucinations are mostly on nested JSON fields (arrays) — structured tokenization seems brittle to tiny logit shifts.
Grace: Repro strategy?
Ishaan: 1) Reproduce deterministically with same calib table + same batching config. 2) Try with kernel steering disabled (force kernel selection to single precision path) 3) Run eval with forced cache warm (prefill) to rule out eviction effect.
Priya: I started a repro job: `repro/run_eval.sh --calib=canary_v2 --force-kernel=fp8 --batch-window=8 --seed=42`. Running now on a 4 GPU toy cluster.
Ryan: I'll export KV telemetry and compare key->idx assignments between baseline and canary for the failing prompts.
Grace: If we can show cache churn correlates with hallucination path, short-term mitigation is to rollback autosteer flag and restore batch window. Can we toggle flag quickly?
Ishaan: Yes, flag toggle in config service -> will disable for prod-serving group B. I'll prepare a rollback patch.
Marta: Also add a one-off eval job that runs the structured-output checklist with both fp8-int4 mixing and all-fp8/all-int4 so we can isolate.
Priya: Early results from my run: quality improved when forced to fp8-only, but int4-only also had fewer hallucinations than mixed. Suggests mixing boundary is the issue.
Ryan: KV diffs show that eviction timing moved some cached KV segments to different GPU shards under the new batching window — so the same prompt gets different shard placement -> slight latency in retrieval -> timing/order difference that changes RNG usage earlier in decode.
Grace: That RNG/timing hypothesis matches why structured outputs are brittle.
Ishaan: Action items:
- Ishaan: roll back mixprecision_autosteer for group B now (toggle + announce) — target 10m
- Priya: run the systematic eval across kernels (fp8-only, int4-only, mixed) with prefills — due in 2h
- Ryan: produce shard-assignment diffs and KV eviction traces for 100 failing prompts — due in 4h
- Marta: add a guard in autosteer to avoid mixing kernel types within the same micro-batch until we fix allocator determinism — create draft PR
- Grace: coordinate a canary rollback if we confirm correlation; help with comms
Ishaan: Rolling the toggle now. Will post update in ~5m. @channel please avoid further deploys to group B until we confirm.
deploy-bot: Rollback request accepted for config service. Rolling back flag mixprecision_autosteer on group B. Est. 2m.
Priya: Nice. My fp8-only run completed: structured-output diff score returned to baseline. Uploading artifacts to //artifacts/triage/1732509999/
Ryan: KV diffs uploaded to same bucket. Early look confirms shard deltas around token positions ~12-18.
Marta: Draft PR with simple micro-batch kernel-homogeneity guard -> pushing to review.
Grace: Thanks. Once we have the full eval matrix and KV diffs we'll decide next steps (fix allocator or change batching heuristics). For now rollback stays.
Ishaan: Update: flag rolled back. Canary metrics trending back to baseline. Leaving this thread open until eval matrix and diffs are in.
